review: Reviewed Moss's round-32 request (functional food preservation) and the accepted world-57 develop review (learning 4): whole-food air-drying on a validated, stable, uncontaminated stone support with conserved water and non-water components, food-specific moisture transport, heat-bounded evaporation, a local air-moisture and heat exchange state and a moisture-dependent spoilage rule, all with explicit numeric parameters. Correction of the development-4 record: it stated that no defensible food moisture model exists in this world; that was incomplete. The ex10 package measured-food-preservation@1 (open-preservation-physics.ts) holds a reviewed water-fraction, evaporation, rain and deterioration model for this world family. It is bound to ex10's food-assay tray apparatus and source-bound items through a three-package chain, so installing it here would require deciding a new support representation. Inspection for this request found that stone records carry only mass, hardness and moisture, with no shape, exposed area or cleanliness, so the reviewed stone support cannot be validated, and that defining one, together with heat exchange, would add new physical rules. Under this run's operating rule the developer does not author new physical rules, so implemented air-dry-food@1 in scope long-ex14 as a general first release, following weather-barrier@1. Set-up performs real checks of the named food (owned, unspoiled, nontoxic) and support (an owned stone piece, or a stone source and whether it is in reach), then fails with the exact report and the unsupported conditions; nothing is reserved, moved or spent and food keeps its existing decay. Inspect, retrieve, resume and cancel fail at no cost because no batch can exist. No preservation, safety claim or reward is added. Blockers recorded for the human: a support geometry representation and the decision to install or adapt the ex10 moisture model. Tests cover the food and support report, unchanged stacks and energy, and failure of every other mode.
